AI can absorb much of the repetitive, structurable work of Data Entry Keyers, but judgment, accountability, and interpersonal coordination still rest with people. What actually gets squeezed out is pure execution.

According to the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS), about 141,600 Data Entry Keyers were employed in 2024, declining to a projected 104,900 by 2034. That represents about 36,700 fewer jobs, with roughly 9,500 openings per year. Median annual pay was about $39,800 in 2026 (BLS OOH, 2026).

AI will not eliminate Data Entry Keyers, but it will reshape their workflow. Tools take repetitive, structured tasks, while people focus on judgment, accountability, and improvement. Scripted execution faces the greatest pressure; workers who understand real operating contexts and make decisions become more valuable.
